For the stated range \(d\ge3\), \(a>0\), the exponent calculation is correct:
\[
a^{2/(d-2)}\epsilon^{1/(d-1)}
=a^{\,2/(d-2)-d/((d-2)(d-1))}
=a^{1/(d-1)}.
\]
The positive sequence \(V_n\) from Theorem 1.1(ii), rescaled as \(v_n=a^{-2/(d-2)}V_n\), satisfies the normalized recurrence with \(\epsilon>0\). The asymptotic assertion of Theorem 1.3 therefore applies and gives exactly the displayed limit for \(V_n\). No additional growth assumption or appeal to uniqueness is needed.
